page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-192GB is a high-density instance within the Cloud Native family, built on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration supplies 64 physical cores across 64 vCPUs with a single thread per core, operating under a shared CPU allocation model on a KVM hypervisor. System memory totals 192 GB, providing an allocation of 3.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and does not feature dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded compute performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 58712.68, alongside elevated results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 402.46 GB/sec and Geekbench ray tracing at 55618.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers at 115.98 GB/sec for reads and 62.73 GB/sec for writes. The primary performance limitation is single-thread execution speed, where stress-ng single-core performance scores in the lower percentile tier due to the conservative 2.0 GHz clock speed.

The shared CPU allocation combined with the absence of included local disks creates a cost-efficient deployment profile for scale-out applications that do not require dedicated hardware cores. Best-fit use cases include multi-threaded batch computation, large-scale CI/CD software compilation, microservices deployments, and distributed background processing tasks.
description: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-192GB is a compute-dense virtual machine within the Cloud Native server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor, it features 64 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz paired with 192 GB of memory, yielding 3.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is provisioned on KVM without bundled local storage or dedicated graphics processing units. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate robust multi-core execution, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 58712.68 and strong multi-threaded decompression rates. However, single-core stress-ng benchmarks reflect lower performance consistent with its base operating frequency. Utilizing shared CPU scheduling without attached disk overhead, this server offers a cost-effective platform for parallelized workloads such as continuous integration build clusters, parallel software compilation, containerized services, and distributed batch processing.
